english.title: Bribe a foreign public official
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intending to obtain or retain business or an advantage in the conduct of business, bribed a foreign public official, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC OFFICIAL..), with the intention of influencing

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

capacity as a foreign public official
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6 and 11 of the Bribery Act 2010.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intending to obtain / retain business / advantage in the conduct of business
bribed a foreign public official with the intention of influencing
his/her capacity as a foreign public official

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(4) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides an explanation of the capacity of a foreign public official.
(ii) Section 6(5) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides a definition of the term "foreign public official".
(iii) Section 6(6) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides a definition of "Public international organisation".
(iv) Section 6(7) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides an explanation of the term "written law".
(v) Section 6(8) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides that for this purposes of this offence a trade or profession is a business.
(vi) 12 months is to be read as 6 months in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003.

other.penalty:
Summary: 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
12 months is to be read as 6 months in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
